correctness.rationale: A singleton needs only an unbordered word. For any code, length-one exclusions force opposite endpoints within each word and a common first symbol across words; bit complementation preserves both conditions. This proves the one-orientation reduction. With self-overlaps excluded at vertex construction and both ordered overlaps excluded at each edge, a clique is exactly a feasible code. In the supplied search, every color class is independent, so after removing later vertices the remaining improvement is bounded by the current color index. Branching on a vertex and restricting the child to its neighbors covers every potentially improving clique. I independently built the bitwise graph for both orientations, with fresh upper-bound search and witnesses, recovering all 55 target values and all ten d=1 controls. The full n=11 graph had 568 vertices, 284 in each orientation. The n=11 row at d=2..11 is (42,14,10,4,2,2,2,1,1,1); A(10,1),A(10,2),A(11,1),A(11,2)=(24,23,44,42). All 55 frozen certificates were separately checked against both ordered overlaps, self-overlap, the exact lengths, cardinality and Hamming distances. The two single-deletion comparisons in RESULT.md also check directly. Replay /workspace/review-work/frontier.py 2 11 1, saved output frontier_results.txt. This verifies binary aligned Hamming constraints only, not frame recovery after a substitution.

value.rationale: The joint optimization is motivated by simultaneous strict synchronization constraints and within-block substitution tolerance. The complete short-block profiles identify exactly where even distance-two enforcement costs codewords and give a sharp n=11 aligned one-substitution capacity of 14, not obtainable from the known unconstrained optimum or generic separation bound. Some high-distance cells are immediate from the orientation, and A(9,2) was known; neither supplies the salient remaining optima. The checked profiles are useful design benchmarks without asserting synchronization under corruptions at unknown boundaries.
